summary: Willamette National Forest lookout site in Lane County: 1919-1920 newspaper items name women lookouts on Winberry Mountain. No build, fate or site record found.

events.note: Nell Southworth spent her summer vacation time on 'Winbury Butte' (1919 season, per a July 4, 1920 Oregonian item); the item does not say she was a lookout
Clara Holbrook named among women working as lookouts 'on Winberry mountain' (July 8, 1920 Morning Register item); the item does not give the season

evidence.supports: 1919 season label on the July 4, 1920 Oregonian item
1920 Oregonian item: Nell Southworth spent summer vacation time on Winbury Butte in the Cascade national forest
evidence.quote: In the Cascade national forest in Oregon was Miss Nell Southworth, a student at the State university, who spent her summer vacation time on Winbury Butte.

evidence.supports: 1920 Morning Register item: Clara Holbrook among women working as lookouts on Winberry mountain
evidence.quote: July 8, 1920: Among the women at work as lookouts, Miss Clara Holbrook on Winberry mountain.

notes_for_editor: Only source is one page of two 1920 newspaper quotations; no build date, design, height, fate or site description found. The name is spelled Winbury Butte in the Oregonian item and Winberry mountain in the Morning Register item; the sources do not show whether they are the same peak. The page names the Willamette National Forest, but the 1920 item calls it the Cascade national forest in Oregon; the naming change was not checked. Searches for the 1991 Willamette NRHP lookout eligibility report found a catalog record but not the PDF, so that report was not checked for Winberry. A 2021 University of Oregon PDF on Willamette lookouts was searched in full text for Winberry and Winbury with no match. Status and access left unknown. Staffing is from the 1920 items only and may not reflect later seasons.
